title: Astrid and the Cover
premise: Gideon Okafor, a gifted interpreter who has spent years making powerful people's words disappear, works out of a nondescript safe house attached to a doomed peace delegation. When the property appears on a real estate site with interior photos — including one showing a document she was ordered to destroy — she realizes someone inside her own circle is selling her out. To survive, she must trade the one secret worth killing for: proof that the peace talks were sabotaged by the very mediator brokering them. In the end, Gideon chooses truth over the loyalty that kept her invisible, exposes the mediator at the delegation's final session, and walks away from the cover of anonymity into a dangerous but honest new life.
about_author: Zephyrine Montrose is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in closed-door negotiations across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the people history forgets to credit — the ones in the room who translate, record, and remember.

chapters.title: The Room Where Words Go to Die
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She interprets a hostile preliminary session of the peace delegation, softening a threat that could collapse everything. We see her skill and her philosophy: she is furniture, invisible, safe. The emotional beat is quiet professional pride shadowed by loneliness.

chapters.title: Number Fourteen, Unlisted
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She returns to the safe house and finds a real estate flyer in her mailbox — the house is listed for sale, with interior photos. One shows her work desk and a folder she was told to burn. Panic sets in beneath her practiced calm.

chapters.title: Protocol of Disappearance
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, with a flashback to how she was recruited by delegation security chief Marek Voss. She reviews the rules that kept her invisible for six years and realizes every rule has been quietly broken. The beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Mediator's Smile
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the delegation's second session, she interprets for Henrik Alvarsson, the celebrated mediator, and notices a phrase he uses that matches wording from the supposedly destroyed document. She says nothing — and hates herself for it.

chapters.title: Who Else Has Keys
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Marek POV. Marek runs an internal sweep for leaks while Gideon quietly inventories who could have photographed the house: Marek, the driver Tomas, the archivist Lena, or Alvarsson's aide. Trust begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Tomas Drives at Night
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The delegation's driver makes an unexplained midnight trip to the safe house. Gideon follows him and watches him photograph the exterior. Confronted, he claims he was paid anonymously — but he kept the payment app's metadata.

chapters.title: The Listing Agent
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She tracks down the realtor, who is baffled: the listing was placed by a brokerage that doesn't exist. The photos were taken with a lens she recognizes from delegation equipment. The beat: the trap is professional, not opportunistic.

chapters.title: Lena's Archive
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The archivist, lonely and observant, has noticed Gideon's fear and offers an unlikely alliance. Lena reveals that pages of the official record have been altered — the sabotage of the talks was written in before it happened.

chapters.title: What the Document Says
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Reconstructing the destroyed folder from memory and Lena's drafts, she confirms it contains proof Alvarsson scripted the talks' failure on behalf of a weapons consortium. She now holds the secret worth killing for.

chapters.title: An Offer, Politely Made
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A stranger buys her coffee and offers her a new identity, a new country, and silence. She understands the offer is also a warning. She stalls, buying forty-eight hours. The beat: terror wearing a courteous mask.

chapters.title: Marek's Blind Spot
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. The security chief discovers the leak traces through his own credentials and realizes he's being framed. His loyalty to the delegation collides with his loyalty to Gideon, whom he recruited and swore to protect.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Someone enters the safe house while she's out and takes nothing — except the original listing photos' timestamp, proving the pictures were taken months ago, before the document even existed. The listing was bait all along.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, introspective. Trapped between exposing Alvarsson and preserving the fragile talks that might still save lives, she weighs justice outside the law against the loyalty that gave her a place to belong. She decides to move.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Botanical Garden
chapters.summary: Gideon and Lena's POV. They copy the reconstructed proof to two hidden locations. Lena is followed; Gideon watches her walk into a trap and must choose between saving the archive and saving her friend.

chapters.title: What Lena Knew
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Lena is hospitalized after a staged accident and can't remember what she hid or where. Guilt and grief sharpen Gideon's resolve. Tomas, terrified, gives her the payment metadata that points to Alvarsson's aide.

chapters.title: The Aide Confesses, Sort Of
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. She corners the aide, Ilse, who admits to the listing and the pressure campaign but claims Alvarsson believes he is saving more lives than the sabotage will cost. The beat: the enemy is sincere, which is worse.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Marek's POV. Marek, cleared of suspicion but stripped of authority, chooses Gideon over the institution and helps her plan to expose Alvarsson at the final session — knowing it will end both their careers and possibly their lives.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Collapse
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The final session begins; Alvarsson's closing script is designed to blame one delegation and detonate the peace process on live broadcast. Gideon must interpret it faithfully while waiting for her moment. Tension at its peak.

chapters.title: The Word She Chose
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, climax. Instead of softening Alvarsson's fatal phrase, she translates it exactly as written — and then, off-script, interprets the sabotaged record aloud in three languages. The room erupts; the broadcast carries every word.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Three Languages
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Alvarsson is detained; Ilse cooperates; the consortium's fingerprints surface. Marek takes the institutional fall to shield Gideon. Lena, recovering, remembers where the second copy is hidden. The cost is counted.

chapters.title: The House Sells
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The safe house finally sells to an ordinary family. Gideon watches the movers carry out furniture that was never hers and feels, for the first time, that invisibility was never safety — only a smaller kind of cage.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, resolution. She adopts the name Astrid — the identity on the forged passport she refuses to use for hiding and chooses instead as a beginning. She signs on as an interpreter for a truth commission, visible at last, and belongs to no cover but her own.
